text:
lily_pr: Heads-up: NYT used 'up to 40% cost reduction' in the headline for our Optimize piece. Our published average is ~34% and the headline implies typical. Should we ask for a clarification? :thinking:

dan_engineering: 34% is the mean; 40% was the max on one workload. Recommend asking for 'average ~34%' in headline.

jasmin_marketing: If they change it, we'll update social and the benchmark page. Also need a 1-paragraph note for Sales to forward.

olivia_ops: If reporter wants data, I can provide a redacted table (no hostnames or customer IDs).

lily_pr: Draft to reporter: "Hi — quick suggested headline clarification: 'Redwood Optimize reduces inference costs by an average of ~34%; peak savings up to 40% on select workloads.' Happy to share a redacted methodology table."

press_bot: reporter_email_delivered: true

lily_pr: Reporter replied: "We'll discuss with the editor, please paste a one-line we can use." Pasted sentence above.

jasmin_marketing: Preparing sales blurb now and updating landing page copy. ETA 30m.

press_bot: article_update_detected: https://www.nytimes.com/example-corrected

lily_pr: NYT updated headline to 'Redwood Optimize cuts inference costs by an average of about 34%'. Editor's note links to our methodology. Loop closed. :white_check_mark:
